What is a loyalty ability and how is it activated?

A loyalty ability is an activated ability with a loyalty symbol in its cost. It can be activated by a player any time they have priority and the stack is empty during a main phase of their turn, provided none of that permanent’s loyalty abilities have been activated that turn. See rules 209.2 and 606, “Loyalty Abilities.”

What is a subgame in Magic: The Gathering and how is it initiated?

A subgame is a completely separate Magic game created by an effect, initiated by a card like Shahrazad. When a subgame starts, an entirely new set of game zones is created, and each player takes all the cards in their main-game library, moves them to their subgame library, and shuffles them. Randomly determining which player goes first, the subgame proceeds like a normal game, following all other rules in rule 103, “Starting the Game.” This is detailed in rules 729.1a and 729.2.

Text used to indicate that the game, for some specific purpose, treats a condition as true even though it’s not. See rule 609.4.

What happens when the top card of a player's planar deck is turned face up in a Planechase game?

If the top card is a phenomenon card, the player puts that card on the bottom of their planar deck and repeats the process until a plane card is turned face up. The face-up plane card becomes the starting plane. (See rule 901.5 and rule 103.7.)

What does "Assign Combat Damage" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
To determine how an attacking or blocking creature will deal its combat damage. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

What happens if an effect would set the life total of each player on a team to a number in a Two-Headed Giant game?
Each team chooses one of its members to be affected. The chosen player on the team with the higher life total loses life to match the lower life total. This is governed by rule 810.9d.

What is the color identity of a card in the Commander variant, and how is it determined?

The color identity of a card in the Commander variant is determined by the color or colors of any mana symbols in the card’s mana cost or rules text, plus any colors defined by its characteristic-defining abilities (509.4) or color indicator (204). It is established before the game begins (509.4a) and is used to determine what cards can be in a deck with a certain commander. Reminder text is ignored when determining a card’s color identity (509.4c), and the back face of a double-faced card is included when determining a card’s color identity (509.4d).

What are the characteristics of a double-faced card when it is outside the game or in a zone other than the battlefield or stack?
A double-faced card outside the game or in a zone other than the battlefield or stack has only the characteristics of its front face. (712.8a)

What happens to the position of a name sticker on an object as it moves between public zones?

The position of each name sticker on an object is remembered as the object moves from one public zone to another, and it continues to apply to the new object it becomes in that zone. This is an exception to rule 400.7. (See rule 123.6c)

A copy of an ability refers to the same object by name as the original ability, as stated in rule 707.10b.

If multiple replacement effects could be applied to the event of a melded permanent leaving the battlefield or being put into the new zone, applying one of those replacement effects to one of the two cards affects both cards. This is governed by rule 712.21d.

Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life. (Rule 120.3a)

What does "Champion, Championed" mean in Magic: The Gathering?

“Champion” is a keyword ability that lets one creature temporarily replace another. A permanent is “championed” by another permanent if the latter exiles the former as the direct result of a champion ability. See rule 702.72, “Champion.”

What does "Continuous Effect" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
An effect that modifies characteristics of objects, modifies control of objects, or affects players or the rules of the game, for a fixed or indefinite period. See rule 611, “Continuous Effects.”

What does "Persist" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that can return a creature from the graveyard to the battlefield. See rule 702.79, “Persist.”

What is a player's devotion to a color or combination of colors in Magic: The Gathering?

A player’s devotion to a color or combination of colors is equal to the number of mana symbols of that color or colors among the mana costs of permanents that player controls. This is calculated after considering any effects that modify devotion, but before any other effects that modify the characteristics of permanents. (Rules 700.5 and 700.5a)

What happens if the game enters a loop of mandatory actions in a multiplayer game?

If the game enters a loop of mandatory actions, the game is a draw for each player who controls an object involved in that loop, as well as for each player within the range of influence of any of those players. They leave the game, and all remaining players continue to play the game. This is described in rule 801.16.

A keyword action. “Waterbend [cost]” means to pay that cost and, for each {1} in that cost, you may tap an untapped artifact or creature you control rather than pay mana. See rule 701.67, “Waterbend.”

A keyword ability that can have a creature enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters on it. See rule 702.82, “Devour.”

What does the term 'stored result' mean in the context of rolling dice on a permanent in Magic: The Gathering?

To store the result of a die roll on a permanent means to note both the kind of die rolled and the result of that roll. That noted information is considered a ‘stored result’ of that permanent, and the result is the ‘value’ of that stored result. (See rule 606.8a)

What is the maximum number of lands a player can play in a single turn, and under what conditions can this number be increased?
A player can normally play one land during their turn, but this number can be increased by continuous effects. The specific rule that describes this is 305.2.

What are the three types of abilities mentioned in the rules text and what do they do?

The three types of abilities mentioned are activated abilities, triggered abilities, and static abilities. Activated abilities have a cost and an effect, triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect, and static abilities create continuous effects while the permanent with the ability is on the battlefield or in the appropriate zone. Citations: 113.3b, 113.3c, 113.3d.

What is the final step in a damage event according to the rules text?
The damage event occurs. This is stated in rule 120.4d, which says 'Finally, the damage event occurs.'

What is a color indicator and how is it represented on a card?

A color indicator is a characteristic of an object, represented by a circular symbol filled in with one or more colors, printed to the left of the type line directly below the illustration on nonland cards without a mana cost. It denotes the color or colors of the object. (See rules 204.1 and 204.2)

What is the starting life total for a player in a Vanguard game, and how does it change based on the vanguard card's life modifier?

The starting life total for a player in a Vanguard game is 20 plus or minus the life modifier of their vanguard card. For example, if a player’s vanguard card has a life modifier of -3, their starting life total is 17. This is described in rule 902.4.

What does "Craft" mean in Magic: The Gathering?

Craft is an activated ability that allows a player to exile cards from their graveyard and/or permanents they control to exile the permanent with the craft ability and return it onto the battlefield transformed. See rule 702.167, “Craft.”

What is the purpose of italicized text in the text box of a Magic card?

Italicized text in the text box of a Magic card can serve as reminder text, flavor text, or ability words. Reminder text summarizes a rule that applies to the card and appears within parentheses, flavor text adds artistic appeal to the game, and ability words are similar to keywords, tying together cards with similar functionality. (509.1a, 207.2a, 207.2b, 207.2c)

What does "Beginning of Combat Step" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
Part of the turn. This step is the first step of the combat phase. See rule 507, “Beginning of Combat Step.”

An italicized word with no rules meaning that ties together abilities on different cards that have similar functionality. See rule 207.2c.

What is the defense number on a battle card and how does it affect the card when it enters the battlefield?

The defense number on a battle card indicates its defense while it’s not on the battlefield, and it also indicates that the battle enters the battlefield with that many defense counters on it. This is specified in rule 210.1. Additionally, the intrinsic ability that causes a battle to enter the battlefield with a number of defense counters on it equal to its printed defense number is described in rule 310.4b.

What does "Ending Phase" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
Part of the turn. This phase is the fifth and final phase of the turn. See rule 512, “Ending Phase.”

That target is ignored; its last known information is not used. This is according to rule 115.9b.

What is a token in Magic: The Gathering according to the rules text provided?

A token is a game object that is subject to anything that affects permanents in general or that affects the token’s card type or subtype. A token isn't a card, even if it is represented by a card with a Magic back or from a booster pack. (Rule 111.6)

What does the expansion symbol on a card indicate, and what are the different colors and their meanings?

The expansion symbol on a card indicates the rarity of the card within its set. A red-orange symbol indicates the card is mythic rare, a gold symbol indicates the card is rare, a silver symbol indicates the card is uncommon, a black or white symbol indicates the card is common or is a basic land, and a purple symbol signifies a special rarity, as seen in the Time Spiral™ “timeshifted” cards. These symbols are found in rule 206.2.

What does the term 'alternate name' refer to in the context of Magic: The Gathering, and how is it used in game rules?

An alternate name is a different name used on promotional or alternate-art versions of some cards. In game rules, instances of the alternate name that are present refer to the name specified in the secondary title bar, which is the card’s name as listed in the Oracle card reference. For the purposes of deck construction, game rules, and effects, these cards have only the card name specified in the secondary title bar. Rules text may also refer to a card’s alternate name, but instances of the alternate name have no effect on gameplay. This is governed by rule 201.6.

What is the inherent triggered ability associated with rad counters and how does it work?

The inherent triggered ability associated with rad counters is an exception to rule 113.8. This ability has no source and is controlled by the active player. It triggers at the beginning of each player’s precombat main phase, causing the player to mill a number of cards equal to the number of rad counters they have. For each nonland card milled this way, the player loses 1 life and removes one rad counter from themselves. This ability is described in rule 728.1.

What does "Umbra Armor" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that allows an Aura to protect the permanent it’s enchanting. See rule 702.89, “Umbra Armor.”

What is the monarch in Magic: The Gathering and how is it determined?

The monarch is a designation a player can have in Magic: The Gathering. It is determined by an effect instructing a player to become the monarch. When a player becomes the monarch, the previous monarch ceases to be the monarch. If the monarch leaves the game, the active player becomes the monarch at the same time, or the next player in turn order who can become the monarch. If no player can become the monarch, the game continues with no monarch. This is detailed in rules 725.1, 725.3, and 725.4.

What does "Aftermath" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that lets a player cast one half of a split card only from their graveyard. See rule 702.127, “Aftermath.”

What are the three exceptions for Commander Draft deck construction compared to Commander deck construction?

The three exceptions for Commander Draft deck construction are: (1) A player’s deck must contain at least 60 cards. (2) A player’s deck may include any number of cards from that player’s card pool with the same name. (3) If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Masters, any card which can be a player’s commander by itself and whose color identity includes one or fewer colors is considered to have the partner ability for the purposes of deckbuilding. Citations: 903.13f(1), 903.13f(2), 903.13f(3).

What are the Attack Left and Attack Right options in multiplayer games, and what do they allow a player to do?

The Attack Left Option (803.1a) allows a player to attack only an opponent seated immediately to their left, a planeswalker they control, or a battle they protect. The Attack Right Option (803.1b) allows a player to attack only an opponent seated immediately to their right, a planeswalker they control, or a battle they protect. These options are used in certain multiplayer variants and are optional. If a player’s nearest opponent is more than one seat away, they can’t attack.

What does "Afterlife" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that leaves behind Spirit creature tokens when certain creatures die. See rule 702.135, “Afterlife.”

The player removes that dungeon card from the game. (See rule 309.6)

What happens if a team has fifteen or more poison counters in a game of Magic: The Gathering?
The team loses the game. (Rule 810.8d)

What is the power and toughness of a creature card with a power and toughness of 2/3, and how can these values be modified according to the rules?

The power and toughness of a creature card with a power and toughness of 2/3 are 2 and 3, respectively. These values can be modified by effects. For example, Lost Order of Jarkeld has power and toughness each equal to 1+*, and its power and toughness are determined by a characteristic-defining ability, which is a type of ability. Such abilities are worded '[This creature’s] power and toughness are each equal to . . .' and function everywhere, even outside the game. (See rules 208.2a and 604.3)

The term 'dies' means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.' (See rule 700.4)

An older name for nonmodal double-faced cards. See rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards.”

What is a permanent in Magic: The Gathering?

A permanent is a card or token on the battlefield. A permanent’s characteristics are the same as those printed on its card, as modified by any continuous effects. Permanents remain on the battlefield indefinitely. A permanent’s owner is the same as the owner of the card that represents it, and a permanent’s controller is, by default, the player under whose control it entered the battlefield. Permanents have four status categories: tapped/untapped, flipped/unflipped, face up/face down, and phased in/phased out. Specific permanent types include artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, land, and planeswalker. The term 'permanent card' refers to a card that could be put onto the battlefield, and the term 'permanent spell' refers to a spell that will enter the battlefield as a permanent as part of its resolution. Rule numbers cited: 110.1, 110.3, 110.4, 110.5.

What does "Unblockable (Obsolete)" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A term that meant “can’t be blocked.” Cards that used this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

What is the Brawl option in Commander games and how does it affect the first mulligan a player takes?

The Brawl option in Commander games is an option for the casual variant. In any Brawl game, the first mulligan a player takes doesn’t count toward the number of cards that player will put on the bottom of their library or the number of mulligans that player may take. This is specified in rule 903.12g.

What happens when an effect that allows something to happen directly contradicts another effect that prevents it from happening?
The effect that prevents it from happening takes precedence. This is described in rule 101.2.

What is the difference between an effect that sets a characteristic and an ability granted by an effect?

An effect that sets a characteristic of an object is not granting an ability. Instead, it defines a characteristic of the object, such as 'Runeclaw Bear is red' or 'Runeclaw Bear can’t be blocked.' This is different from an ability granted by an effect, which can be removed by another effect. (See rules 113.12 and 604.3)

What happens if a multiplayer game using the limited range of influence option is restarted?

If a multiplayer game using the limited range of influence option is restarted, all players in the game are involved, regardless of the range of influence of the player who controls the ability that restarted the game. (727.7)

What does "Entwine" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that lets a player choose all modes for a spell rather than just the number specified. See rule 702.42, “Entwine.”

A characteristic that only vanguards have. See rule 212, “Life Modifier.”

What does "Shadow" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked and which creatures it can block. See rule 702.28, “Shadow.”

What happens when a double-faced card is turned face down?

When a double-faced card is turned face down, it remains hidden, using a face-down substitute card (see rule 713) and/or opaque sleeves. It can’t transform or convert, and if it’s turned face up, it will have its front face up (see rule 712.15a).

What does "Forecast" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A keyword ability that allows an activated ability to be activated from a player’s hand. See rule 702.57, “Forecast.”

What does "Activated Ability" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A kind of ability. Activated abilities are written as “[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]” See rule 113, “Abilities,” and rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

What is the Grand Melee variant and how many players typically use it?

The Grand Melee variant is a modification of the Free-for-All variant, used in games with ten or more players. It uses default options such as a range of influence of 1, the attack left option, and does not use the attack multiple players and deploy creatures options. Rule 807.1 provides this information.

What are the parts of a card and how do they relate to an object's characteristics?

The parts of a card include name, mana cost, illustration, color indicator, type line, expansion symbol, text box, power and toughness, loyalty, defense, hand modifier, life modifier, illustration credit, legal text, and collector number. Some of these parts are also characteristics of the object, such as name, mana cost, color, color indicator, card type, subtype, supertype, rules text, abilities, power, toughness, loyalty, defense, hand modifier, and life modifier. See rules 200.1, 200.2, 109.3, and 105 for more details.

What does "Spell Type" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
A subtype that’s correlated to the instant card type and the sorcery card type. See rule 304, “Instants,” and rule 307, “Sorceries.” See rule 205.3k for the list of spell types.

What conditions must be met for a permanent to transform or convert according to the rules?

Only permanents represented by double-faced tokens and double-faced cards that are not meld cards can transform or convert. (See rule 712.9) If a spell or ability instructs a player to transform or convert a permanent that isn’t represented by a double-faced token or a double-faced card, nothing happens. (See rule 712.9) If a double-faced card or a copy of a double-faced card is cast as a spell “transformed” or “converted,” it’s put on the stack with its back face up. (See rule 712.11a) A player casting a modal double-faced card or a copy of a modal double-faced card as a spell chooses which face they are casting before putting it onto the stack. (See rule 712.11b) Only the face that will be face up on the stack is evaluated to determine if it can be cast. (See rule 712.11c) If an ability of a double-faced card’s front face allows it to be cast “transformed” or “converted,” that ability is also considered when evaluating that spell to determine if it can be cast. (See rule 712.11d)

What happens when a player loses the game in a tournament setting?
When a player loses the game in a tournament, that player leaves the game. This is stated in rule 104.5.104.5

What happens when a name sticker is placed on an object in Magic: The Gathering?

When a name sticker is placed on an object, the object’s controller chooses a position in the object’s name for the word in the name sticker to be added, then announces the object’s new name. The new name can be at the beginning of the object’s name or after any number of the other words that are currently in its name. The new name can be further modified by other name stickers. If the object has no name, its name becomes the word added by the name sticker. (509.6b)

What does "Commander" mean in Magic: The Gathering?

1. A casual variant in which each deck is led by a legendary card (usually a creature). See rule 903, “Commander.” 2. A designation given to one legendary card in each player’s deck in the Commander casual variant.

What is the Free-for-All multiplayer variant and how is it played?

In the Free-for-All multiplayer variant, players compete as individuals against each other. The limited range of influence option is usually not used, and the attack left, attack right, or attack multiple players options must be used. The deploy creatures option is not used. Players are randomly seated around the table. See rules 806.1, 806.2, and 806.3.

What is the commander tax and when can a player cast their commander from the command zone?

The commander tax is an additional cost of {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game. A player may cast a commander they own from the command zone, and this cost is in addition to the mana cost of the card. This is specified in rule 903.8.

What happens to stickers on an object when it moves to a hidden zone?
Stickers on an object are not retained as that object moves to a hidden zone. (123.5)

What is the difference between an Equipment and a Fortification in terms of attachment and control?

An Equipment’s controller is separate from the equipped creature’s controller, and changing control of the creature doesn’t change control of the Equipment, and vice versa. Only the Equipment’s controller can activate its abilities. Fortifications are similar, but they can only be attached to lands, and a Fortification that’s also a creature can’t fortify a land. (See rules 301.5d and 301.6)

What are the subtypes for an artifact card, and how are they different from other card types?

Artifact cards have their own unique set of subtypes called artifact types, which include Attraction, Blood, Bobblehead, Book, Clue, Contraption, Equipment, Food, Fortification, Gold, Incubator, Infinity, Junk, Lander, Map, Mutagen, Powerstone, Spacecraft, Stone, Treasure, Vehicle, and Vibranium. These artifact types are distinct from the subtypes of other card types, which are listed after a long dash and can be one or two words. For example, an artifact card can be a ‘Artifact — Equipment’ or ‘Artifact — Treasure’, but it cannot be a ‘Artifact — Forest’ as Forest is a land type. (See rules 205.3b, 205.3d, and 205.3g)

What are the characteristics of Conspiracy cards in the command zone?

Conspiracy cards in the command zone are not permanents and cannot be cast or included in a deck. They have no subtypes and their static or triggered abilities affect the game as long as they are face up. Rule 315.3 and Rule 315.4 provide these details.

What does "Hybrid Card" mean in Magic: The Gathering?
